name: Tobramycin
executiveSummary: Antipseudomonal aminoglycoside. Adult/pediatric IV: **5–7 mg/kg/day** (traditional q8h) or **5–7 mg/kg every 24 h** (extended interval). CF often **10 mg/kg every 24 h**. Inhaled: **300 mg every 12 h** (cycles). Monitor levels and creatinine.
indications:
## Indications

- Serious Gram-negative infections (esp. *Pseudomonas*) in combination.
- Cystic fibrosis: IV and/or inhaled (TOBI and others).

## Precautions

- Nephro- and ototoxicity — levels (peak/trough or AUC) and renal function.
- Adjust by CrCl; caution with other nephrotoxins.
- Do not mix in the same syringe with β-lactams (inactivation).

> Prefer extended interval in many non-CF adults per PK protocol.

adulto.dose: Conventional IV: **1.5–2.5 mg/kg every 8 h** (**~5–7 mg/kg/day**). Extended interval: **5–7 mg/kg IV every 24 h**. CF: often **10 mg/kg IV every 24 h**. Inhaled: **300 mg every 12 h** in 28-day on/off cycles (specific product).
adulto.administration: IV over 30–60 min in NS/D5W. Nebulize with indicated system; do not mix other drugs in the same cup without protocol.
adulto.notes: Calculate by ideal body weight in obesity per center.

pediatrico.dose: **2–2.5 mg/kg every 8 h** or **5–7.5 mg/kg every 24 h** per protocol. CF: often **10 mg/kg every 24 h**. Inhaled: by age/product (e.g. 300 mg q12h in ≥6 years).

neonatal.dose: Orientative: **4–5 mg/kg/dose every 24–48 h** by PMA/PNA and renal function.

stability:
## Stability

- Diluted IV: ~24 h refrigerated.
- Nebulization: use immediately after opening.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity (cochlear/vestibular), neuromuscular blockade (rare), bronchospasm (inhaled).
